`app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:17`: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` is a substring check, not an origin check. `http://discourse.example.co` is a substring of `http://discourse.example.com`, so an attacker who registers a prefix-substring domain passes. Use an exact comparison against a normalized origin.

`app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:12`: no null check on `document.getElementById('discourse-comments')` — throws a `TypeError` on any page missing the div. Also no `<script>`/usage documentation was added for the two required globals (`discourseUrl`, `discourseEmbedUrl`), and there is no asset-precompile registration for `embed.js`/`embed.css` in the diff (`config/application.rb` isn't in this tree — verify it's there, otherwise `stylesheet_link_tag 'embed'` fails in production).
`app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:8`: height is posted once on `window.onload`; late-loading images/avatars leave the iframe mis-sized, and there is no resize listener.

`app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:20-22`: `feed_key` is dead code — presumably intended for conditional GET (`If-Modified-Since`), which is never wired up. Either implement it or remove it; every hour the full feed is re-fetched and every item re-SHA1'd.
`lib/topic_retriever.rb:26-29`: `setnx` + `expire` is non-atomic; a crash between them leaves a permanent key and permanently blocks retrieval of that URL. Use `set(key, "1", ex: 60, nx: true)`.
`app/models/topic_embed.rb:13`: `contents <<` mutates the caller's string (raises on frozen literals, and pollutes memoized `let(:contents)` across examples). Prefer `contents + ...`.

`app/models/topic_embed.rb:1`: `require_dependency 'nokogiri'` — `require_dependency` is for autoloadable app code, not gems; use `require`. Conversely, `open-uri` is required only in `poll_feed.rb` but `open` is called in `topic_embed.rb:47`; the retriever path can reach it without that file being loaded.
`app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb:1`: `require_dependency 'email/sender'` is unused copy-paste.
`config/locales/server.en.yml`: `embed.permalink` is added but never referenced.

Test coverage gaps: no test for `absolutize_urls` with https/non-default ports or protocol-relative URLs, no test that actually parses a feed fixture in `poll_feed_spec` (everything is mocked at the `poll_feed` boundary), and no `EmbedController` test for a referer whose host *mismatches* `embeddable_host` (only the missing-referer case is covered).

`app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:25`: `X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL` is not a valid directive; it works only because browsers ignore unparseable values. A `Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors <embeddable_host>` would express the intent and actually restrict framing.

goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **3. `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35` + `app/models/post.rb:130` + `app/views/embed/best.html.erb:19` — unsanitized third-party HTML becomes stored XSS**

adjudication.rationale: Yes. `Jobs::PollFeed` imports third‑party feed HTML via `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` and passes it to `TopicEmbed.import` without sanitization. `TopicEmbed.import` stores it as a post with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and `Post#cook` explicitly returns `raw` (skipping the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline) when `cook_method` is `:raw_html`. Finally, the embed template renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, so any script/event-handler HTML from the feed becomes stored and executed when viewed (stored XSS). `absolutize_urls` only rewrites relative `href/src` and does not sanitize.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **4. `app/models/topic_embed.rb:13` — attribute injection in the "Imported from" link**

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicEmbed.import`, the code appends HTML containing an `` tag built via string interpolation: `"#{url}"` and inserts it into `contents`. The only validation is `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which does not prevent quotes or other characters in the remainder of the URL. A crafted URL like `http://example.com/' onmouseover='alert(1)` still matches the regex and would break out of the `href` attribute, enabling attribute injection/XSS. This is especially impactful because imported posts are created with `cook_method: :raw_html`, and `Post#cook` returns `raw` (no sanitization), and the embed view renders with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **5. `app/models/topic_embed.rb:24` — `post.present?` doesn't mean the post saved**

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, `post = creator.create` is immediately followed by `if post.present?` before creating the `TopicEmbed` row. Whether `post.present?` implies persistence depends entirely on `PostCreator#create`’s contract, which is not shown or changed in this diff (the diff only tweaks `setup_post` to copy `cook_method`). Without evidence in the diff that `PostCreator#create` can return a non-nil but unsaved post, the claim is speculative and not a verifiable defect introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **6. `app/models/topic_embed.rb:32-36` — `PostRevisor.new(nil)` when the embedded post was deleted**

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, when an existing `TopicEmbed` record is found (`else` branch), it does `post = embed.post` and then, if the content changed, unconditionally constructs `revisor = PostRevisor.new(post)` and calls `revisor.revise!`. If the associated post has been deleted (the `topic_embeds.post_id` column is non-null but there is no FK/dependent cleanup in this diff), `embed.post` will return `nil`, leading to `PostRevisor.new(nil)` and a runtime error when revising. There is no guard for `post.blank?` before using `PostRevisor`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **7. `app/models/topic_embed.rb:47` — SSRF and unbounded fetch in `import_remote`**

adjudication.rationale: `TopicEmbed.import_remote` does `open(url).read` with no validation of scheme/host and no bounds/timeouts, then feeds the entire body into Readability. This is verifiably an unbounded fetch/DoS risk (large/slow responses can exhaust memory or hang the job). It is also an SSRF-capable primitive in this method as written: unlike `TopicEmbed.import` (which regex-checks `http(s)`), `import_remote` accepts any `url` string and `open-uri` can fetch arbitrary locations; while the `TopicRetriever` path restricts host via `invalid_host?`, `import_remote` is also called directly from the Disqus import task without any host/scheme restriction, so the method itself remains unsafe.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **8. `spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:19-30` — two tests pass vacuously**

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `Jobs::PollFeed#execute`, `poll_feed` only runs if **all** of these are true: `feed_polling_enabled?`, `feed_polling_url.present?`, and `embed_by_username.present?`. In `spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb`, the “requires feed_polling_url” and “requires embed_by_username” examples only stub the respective setting to `nil`, but they do **not** stub `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` to `true`. Since the default setting in `config/site_settings.yml` is `feed_polling_enabled: false`, those specs can pass even if `execute` *never checked* `feed_polling_url` or `embed_by_username`—they pass because the first condition is false (vacuous pass).

adjudication_records.issue_text: **9. `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:47` — `TopicView.expects(:new)` with no `.returns`**

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, `@topic_view` is assigned from `TopicView.new(...)` and then the action implicitly renders the template. In the controller spec shown, there is no `render_views`, so Rails controller specs won’t execute the ERB template that would call methods on `@topic_view`. Under Mocha, `TopicView.expects(:new).with(...)` will return `nil` by default, but the controller action itself does not call any methods on the returned object, so the request can still succeed and the expectation still verifies the call. This is not a verifiable defect introduced by the diff—at most it’s a test-strength/style concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **10. `app/models/topic_embed.rb:75` / `app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:9` — no embed URL normalization**

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The new embed workflow treats `embed_url` as an opaque string everywhere, with exact-match lookups and uniqueness based on the raw string. In `EmbedController#best`, `embed_url = params.require(:embed_url)` is passed directly to `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` and to the background job. `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed` does `where(embed_url: embed_url)` (exact match), and `TopicEmbed.import` uses `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` plus a unique index on `embed_url`. Because there is no canonicalization/normalization (e.g., scheme/host casing, default ports, trailing slashes, fragment removal, query normalization), the same page can map to multiple different `embed_url` strings and thus create multiple topics / miss existing embeds, which is a real correctness defect in the embedding feature.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **12. `db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:4` — an already-shipped migration was edited to add `force: true`**

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show an existing migration file (`db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb`) being modified to add `force: true` to `create_table`. However, the finding’s key claim that this is an "already-shipped" migration cannot be verified from the diff alone, and the change itself is not a clear functional defect in normal Rails operation because migrations are not rerun once applied (so it won’t affect already-migrated DBs). `force: true` would only matter if the migration is executed when the table already exists (e.g., redo/reset/out-of-sync schema), which is not a definite, introduced bug based solely on this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:17`: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` is a substring check, not an origin check. `http://discourse.example.co` is a substring of `http://discourse.example.com`, so an attacker who registers a prefix-substring domain passes. Use an exact comparison against a normalized origin.
matched_golden_ids: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same vulnerability: using `indexOf`/substring matching for origin validation can be bypassed by attacker-controlled domains that contain the trusted domain as a substring (e.g., prefix/similar domain), allowing malicious origins to pass. Candidate also recommends exact/normalized origin comparison, aligning with the golden concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:12`: no null check on `document.getElementById('discourse-comments')` — throws a `TypeError` on any page missing the div. Also no `<script>`/usage documentation was added for the two required globals (`discourseUrl`, `discourseEmbedUrl`), and there is no asset-precompile registration for `embed.js`/`embed.css` in the diff (`config/application.rb` isn't in this tree — verify it's there, otherwise `stylesheet_link_tag 'embed'` fails in production).

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js`, `comments` is assigned via `document.getElementById('discourse-comments')` and is used immediately with `comments.appendChild(iframe);` without checking for null. If the script runs on a page that does not include a `#discourse-comments` element, this will throw a `TypeError` at runtime. The other claims about missing documentation for globals and missing asset precompile registration depend on files/config not shown in the diff and are not directly verifiable here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:8`: height is posted once on `window.onload`; late-loading images/avatars leave the iframe mis-sized, and there is no resize listener.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb`, the iframe posts its height only once via `window.onload`, and there is indeed no listener to re-post height on later layout changes (e.g., parent resize). However, the specific claim that “late-loading images/avatars leave the iframe mis-sized” is not verifiable from this diff: `window.onload` in the iframe fires after the document’s images/resources have finished loading, so initial avatar/image loading should already be accounted for when the height is sent. Any remaining issue would be about *later reflow events* (like resizing), not late-loading images as stated.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:20-22`: `feed_key` is dead code — presumably intended for conditional GET (`If-Modified-Since`), which is never wired up. Either implement it or remove it; every hour the full feed is re-fetched and every item re-SHA1'd.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `feed_key` (lines ~20-22) is defined but never referenced anywhere in the job (`execute` only calls `poll_feed`, and `poll_feed` doesn't use `feed_key`). This is verifiable dead code in the diff. Also, as implemented, `poll_feed` always does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` on each run and iterates all items, calling `TopicEmbed.import` which computes a SHA1 of the contents each time, so there is no conditional/cached fetch mechanism wired up despite the presence of `feed_key`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `lib/topic_retriever.rb:26-29`: `setnx` + `expire` is non-atomic; a crash between them leaves a permanent key and permanently blocks retrieval of that URL. Use `set(key, "1", ex: 60, nx: true)`.

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb#retrieved_recently?, the throttle key is created with `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` and only then given a TTL via `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. These are two separate Redis commands; if the process crashes or the connection drops after `setnx` succeeds but before `expire` runs, the key will persist without an expiration, causing `retrieved_recently?` to return `true` forever for that embed URL and permanently preventing retrieval. Using a single atomic `SET key value NX EX 60` (e.g., `set(retrieved_key, "1", nx: true, ex: 60)`) avoids this failure mode.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/models/topic_embed.rb:13`: `contents <<` mutates the caller's string (raises on frozen literals, and pollutes memoized `let(:contents)` across examples). Prefer `contents + ...`.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, `contents << ...` does indeed mutate the passed-in String. However, the proposed impact is not verifiable from this diff: there is no `frozen_string_literal: true` shown, and the call sites added here (`PollFeed` builds a fresh `content` string, `import_remote` uses `doc.content`) don’t reuse `contents` afterward. Also, the claim about “pollutes memoized `let(:contents)` across examples” is incorrect because RSpec `let` is memoized per-example, not across examples. So this is more of an API/design preference than a clear defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/models/topic_embed.rb:1`: `require_dependency 'nokogiri'` — `require_dependency` is for autoloadable app code, not gems; use `require`. Conversely, `open-uri` is required only in `poll_feed.rb` but `open` is called in `topic_embed.rb:47`; the retriever path can reach it without that file being loaded.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `TopicEmbed.import_remote` which calls `open(url).read` in `app/models/topic_embed.rb` without requiring `open-uri` in that file. The only new `require 'open-uri'` in the diff is in `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, but `import_remote` is also reached via `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` (`lib/topic_retriever.rb`) and from the Disqus thor task, neither of which requires `open-uri`. Without `open-uri`, `Kernel#open` won’t handle HTTP URLs and will typically attempt to open a local file named like `http://...`, causing failures. The note about `require_dependency 'nokogiri'` being intended for reloadable app code is more of a convention/style issue, but the missing `open-uri` requirement is a real, verifiable correctness bug in the new code path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb:1`: `require_dependency 'email/sender'` is unused copy-paste.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb`, the job only looks up a user and calls `TopicRetriever.new(...).retrieve`. There is no reference to `Email::Sender` (or any constant from `email/sender`) anywhere in this new file, so `require_dependency 'email/sender'` appears unnecessary. However, this is a cleanup/style/dead-require issue rather than a verifiable bug/correctness/security defect introduced by the diff (the code will still function without using that dependency).

adjudication_records.issue_text: `config/locales/server.en.yml`: `embed.permalink` is added but never referenced.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds the i18n key `en.embed.permalink` in `config/locales/server.en.yml`, and there is no reference to `t('embed.permalink')`/`I18n.t('embed.permalink')` in the added Ruby/views/JS/CSS. However, an unused translation key is not a verifiable correctness/security bug introduced by this diff; it’s at most dead/unused data and could be intended for future use.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Test coverage gaps: no test for `absolutize_urls` with https/non-default ports or protocol-relative URLs, no test that actually parses a feed fixture in `poll_feed_spec` (everything is mocked at the `poll_feed` boundary), and no `EmbedController` test for a referer whose host *mismatches* `embeddable_host` (only the missing-referer case is covered).

adjudication.rationale:
The diff introduces new behavior in `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls`, `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed`, and `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, but the added specs don’t cover several meaningful cases mentioned.

- `spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb` only asserts URL absolutization for an `http://eviltrout.com/...` URL with default ports and only for paths starting with `/`. There are no tests for `https` or non-default ports (even though `absolutize_urls` has explicit `uri.port` logic) and no handling/tests for protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn...`.
- `spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb` only tests the `execute` guard conditions and that `poll_feed` is invoked; it never exercises `poll_feed` itself (no feed fixture parsing, no `SimpleRSS.parse` / `open` behavior tested), so it’s mocked at the `poll_feed` boundary as the finding states.
- `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb` tests “no referer” and a “success” path where referer matches, but does not include a case where a referer is present and its host mismatches `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, which is a distinct branch in `ensure_embeddable`.

These are concrete, verifiable test coverage gaps in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:25`: `X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL` is not a valid directive; it works only because browsers ignore unparseable values. A `Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors <embeddable_host>` would express the intent and actually restrict framing.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` the code sets `response.headers['X-Frame-Options'] = "ALLOWALL"`. `X-Frame-Options` only standardly supports `DENY` and `SAMEORIGIN` (and the nonstandard/deprecated `ALLOW-FROM` in some browsers); `ALLOWALL` is not a valid directive and will be ignored by compliant browsers. If the app/framework sets a default `X-Frame-Options` elsewhere (commonly `SAMEORIGIN`/`DENY`), this attempt to override it will not achieve the intended embedding behavior, and it also doesn’t actually restrict framing to the configured host. The suggested alternative (`Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors ...`) is a valid way to express host-based framing restrictions.
